summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease status post bypass, diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted due to bradycardia, chest pain, and severe hyperkalemia (K 8.3) detected during a dialysis session. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate, insulin, and kayexalate, followed by hemodialysis. Chest pain episodes occurred during dialysis and resolved with nitroglycerin. Cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction, and a stress MIBI test revealed a stable fixed inferior wall perfusion defect without new ischemia. His medications were adjusted, including reducing metoprolol to 25 mg daily and restarting lisinopril at 2.5 mg daily. Potassium normalized, and he was discharged home in stable condition after six days with follow-up planned with cardiology and nephrology.
